overview: Sprint is a keep-sprint module written in Java inside the otherwise Kotlin client. One UpdateEvent handler decides the sprint flag every tick: the release branch calls setSprinting(false) when the player is stationary, sneaking, blinded, low on food, or (with CheckServerSide) when the real look diverges more than 30 degrees from the rotation target a rotation module is driving; the sprint branch calls setSprinting(true) when AllDirections is on or the forward input is at least 0.8, with one interlock: if Criticals is enabled in HYTJump mode the module stays silent, because Criticals.onUpdate force-clears the sprint flag every tick so the HYTJump launch never becomes a sprint jump. The module never constructs a packet; the C0B traffic comes from the vanilla tick machinery that mirrors the sprint flag to the server.

sections.p: The release branch fires on any of: MovementUtils.isMoving false, the player sneaking, blindness active while the Blindness toggle is on, food at or below 6 without allowFlying while the Food toggle is on, or the CheckServerSide condition. The sprint branch then gates on allDirectionsValue or mc.thePlayer.movementInput.moveForward >= 0.8F, and adds the Criticals interlock: LiquidBounce.moduleManager.getModule(Criticals.class) with getState() true and mode HYTJump suppresses the sprint write entirely, because Criticals.onUpdate sets isSprinting = false every tick in HYTJump and NGJump modes to keep the launch from converting into a sprint jump.

sections.h: Wire presence through the vanilla flag diff
sections.p: setSprinting is a local flag write; the C0B is produced by the tick machinery that compares the flag against the last server-sprint state and emits one START_SPRINTING or STOP_SPRINTING per transition. The LiquidSense Dev snapshot ships no net/minecraft tree, so the fork's EntityPlayerSP cannot be read; the stock 1.8 contract is a per-tick diff that sends at most one C0B per flag change, meaning repeated setSprinting(true) calls with no state change emit nothing. AllDirections backward and sideways sprint only works if the fork honors multi-direction sprint server-side, which is unverifiable in this snapshot, so the honest statement is that the module asks for sprint in every direction and the server decides.

With CheckServerSide on, the module unsprints whenever RotationUtils.targetRotation is set and RotationUtils.getRotationDifference(current yaw and pitch) exceeds 30 degrees, and CheckServerSideOnlyGround narrows that test to grounded ticks. This is the anti-interference switch: while Aura or another rotation module swings the view away from the movement direction, Sprint refuses to claim sprint, because a sprinting player whose motion disagrees with the reported look is a recognizable signature. The food gate mirrors vanilla's own starvation unsprint, so the module's defaults keep it inside the legitimate sprint envelope.

files.label: Sprint.java
files.explanation: The entire module: the release-branch conditions, the sprint-branch write, the Criticals HYTJump interlock, and the CheckServerSide rotation-difference test. It touches only the sprint flag; every C0B on the wire is the vanilla flag-diff machinery's output, which the prose explains because the fork's EntityPlayerSP is absent from this snapshot.

files.label: MovementUtils.java (movement gate)
files.explanation: isMoving is the primary gate every tick: it reads the movement input state and returns false when no direction key is held, which drives the first release-branch condition. It is the movement-domain utility the module leans on, and the same util family powers the Speed and Strafe modules the client pairs with Sprint.

countering.label: ToggleFrequency (C0B rate window)
countering.explanation: The EntityActionAdapter scores every C0B into NetData.playerActionFreq, and ToggleFrequency compares the window against cc.toggleActionLimit, default 25 actions per second, cancelling at vl > 10. The module emits one START per enable and one STOP per gate trip, a handful of C0Bs per second, so it passes by design; this is the wtap counter and auto-sprint volume is not its target. The honest baseline: sprint spam that stays under a few toggles per second is structurally invisible to the rate window.

countering.label: SprintA (hunger gate)
countering.explanation: Grim flags with a setback when player.food is at or below 6.0 while the server sprint state is true, with flying players and camels exempt. The module's own food gate requires foodLevel > 6 or allowFlying before it sprints, so the player never presents a starving sprint to the check: the module and the check share the same threshold, which makes the check a designed non-event here rather than a counter.

countering.label: ActionToggleSpeed (same-tick toggle burst)
countering.explanation: Hawk punishes a sprint toggle whose gap since the previous toggle is under one tick. The vanilla flag diff emits at most one C0B per tick, so the module's STOP and the following START land exactly one tick apart and pass at default; only a same-tick double toggle, the wtap pattern this module does not produce, trips it. The boundary is exact: single per-tick transitions are the check's reward path.

countering.label: EntityAction wrapper (no C0B consumer)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's PacketListener subscribes only FLYING, POSITION, USE_ENTITY, ARM_ANIMATION, HELD_ITEM_SLOT and BLOCK_PLACE, and this C0B wrapper class is never constructed by the anticheat, so the entire sprint surface is invisible to Arc v2. The resolving rel is the wrapper that would carry the packet; the honest statement is that a brief-pinned Arc v2 sprint counter can only be a gap entry.
